description: btauth/1 verify cases (spec 4.3, 11.7). Verify inputs with self_hotkey, now_ns, max_age_s and allowed_skew_s; when inputs.prior is set, verify it first with the same nonce store (it must be accepted). headers is a list of [name, value] pairs, so duplicates can be expressed. expected is the normative answer; python_reference, when present, is what the Python reference does instead and why.

vectors.description: sender SS58 with a bad checksum
target decoded by the router ('/a b' instead of '/a%20b')
ed25519 signature without X-Bittensor-Crypto: verified as sr25519 only, never falls back
<Bytes>-wrapped sr25519 signature (strict: rejected, Python included, D22)
<Bytes>-wrapped ed25519 signature (strict: rejected, Python included, D22)
replay of an accepted request (inputs.prior is the same request, verified first with the same store)
accepted nonce reused with a changed body: the signature fails first, the store is consulted only after step 4
sender SS58 with prefix 0 (Alice's Polkadot address)
sender SS58 with a two-byte prefix (1284)
sender SS58 decodes to 36 bytes (one byte too many)
duplicate nonce header, names differ in case only
signature with an odd number of hex digits
signature hex with an inner space
signature hex with a trailing space (a server that keeps trailing whitespace passes it on)
receiver header is the literal unbound marker '-'
nonce allowed_skew + 1 ns in the future
nonce of 20 digits above the u64 maximum: well-formed, far in the future
notes: Implementations holding the nonce as u64 must report this as stale (step 3), not malformed: the digits are valid.

order: wrong receiver and stale -> receiver first

weak ed25519 key (identity point) with the universal signature
notes: Weak key: the identity point has a signature (R = identity, S = 0) that verifies for every payload. bittensor.http_auth accepts it; kit verifiers in every language reject it as a bad signature, checked after the signature and before the replay store.
